is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles arabiensis.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports Vgsc L995F (L1014F) and Vgsc N1575Y (N1575Y).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides allele frequencies and sample sizes (n alleles) for L1014F and N1575Y across multiple populations and years.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Burkina Faso, Benin, Cameroon, and Ghana.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study involving field collection, sequencing, and genotyping of mosquito populations.

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper specifies collection sites such as Soumousso, Kuinima, Goundry, Malanville, Houeyiho, Bohicon, Tori Bossito, and Accra.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports collection years 2006, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011, with specific data provided for these annual windows.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new collections and original genotyping data.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data for the assessment is contained within the main text and tables of the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This study identifies the N1575Y mutation in the VGSC of Anopheles gambiae s.s. in West/Central Africa, showing it is linked to the L1014F mutation and is under positive selection. It provides allele frequencies for these markers across multiple field sites and years, and demonstrates an additive resistance benefit of the 1014F-1575Y haplotype compared to 1014F-1575N.
